Pittsburgh ranks 30th in the country in opponent-adjusted EPA and 10th in defensive success rate. Meanwhile, Florida State ranks 104th and 102nd in those two metrics. Florida State's best offensive weapon is running the football, but now they have to face a Panthers defense that's fourth in the country in opponent EPA per rush and third in opponent rush success rate. If the Seminoles can't move the ball, it's going to be tough for them to be competitive in a road game against Pittsburgh. I'll lay the points with the home team. Pick: Pittsburgh -3.5 (-108) Illinois vs. UCLA Best Bet UCLA somehow continues to be underrated in the eyes of both football fans and the betting market. The fact that they're rated lower than the two-loss Alabama Crimson Tide is proof of that. The Bruins' defense can carry them a long way this season, ranking fifth in opponent-adjusted EPA per play and second in opponent success rate. Much like Florida State vs. Pittsburgh, this is a game between one of the best defenses in the country and one of the worst. Illinois ranks 131st in defensive success rate, which has hurt them in several games already this season. I'll continue to ride with UCLA in this Big Ten game and bet on them to cover the double-digit spread. Pick: UCLA -10 (-108) Houston vs. Colorado Best Bet Colorado's defense is one-dimensional. They're ninth in the country in opponent EPA per rush, but they're 98th in opponent EPA per pass, meaning when they face a team that relies on an effective run game, the Buffaloes are in a great spot; but then they take on an elite passing attack, they struggle. Unfortunately for them, Houston has one of the best passing games in the country, ranking seventh in EPA per rush and fourth in pass success rate. That, paired with the fact that Colorado has one of the worst offenses in power conference football, leaves Houston in a great spot to cover as road favorites. Illinois has been lifeless on the defensive side of the ball in creating takeaways. A poor Havoc ranking is a product of minimal tackles for loss and a pass rush rank at 121st, per PFF . Dieffenbach is coming off a game with just eight completions for more than 300 yards against Minnesota. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings project UCLA to exceed market expectations, power-rated as an 11-point favorite over Illinois. The Fighting Illini have won four straight and hve qualified for a bowl, taking any pressure off must-win games for a postseason appearance. Look for UCLA's Defensive Havoc and Dieffenbach's explosive passing to cover the number against an Illinois team that has lost big in two previous Big Ten West Coast trips. Pick: UCLA -10 or Better

away.headline: UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach exits game vs. Illinois with apparent injury
away.blurb: A three-star recruit out of Agoura Hills, California, Dieffenbach began his college career at Pittsburgh but didn’t see any game action in his first two seasons. He started 12 games for Cal Poly last year, posting 1,305 passing yards, a 56.8% completition rate, 9 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. UCLA has already weathered one major quarterback injury. It can only hope it’s not facing another. Ty Dieffenbach, a bright spot for the No. 4-ranked Bruins since starter Nico Iamaleava’s knee injury , exited Friday’s game against Illinois with an apparent injury. Third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava, Nico’s brother, replaced him under center with UCLA up 10-0. The injury occurred less than a minute before halftime, when Dieffenbach took a hard hit from Illinois defensive lineman Carter Janki on an incomplete pass. Dieffenbach was writhing on the ground while holding his left shoulder, then had to be helped off the field and into the blue tent. He moved to the locker room at halftime, with a clear limp. There was no sign of him at the start of the third quarter, with Iamaleava continuing to lead the UCLA offense. Dieffenbach transferred to UCLA from Cal Poly last offseason and sat second on the QB depth chart until the elder Iamaleava went down in Week 6 against Oregon. Since then, the Bruins offense has barely missed a beat with Dieffenbach reeling off four straight wins in his first four starts before this week. With a 9-0 record entering Friday, UCLA is in the thick of the College Football Playoff race and is one of two remaining undefeated teams in the FBS, alongside No. 2 Utah. The committee has considered quarterback injuries in the past, potentially adding even more drama for a team whose ranking has been a matter of some controversy .

picks.headline: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 14, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. picks.headline: Texas A&M vs. Tennessee Prediction: Who Wins and Why?
picks.source: Texas A&M Aggies On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: With just three more games to reach bowl eligibility, Texas A&M football is in desperate need of its first ranked win of the season. Despite having one of the Southeastern Conference's best home-field advantages, it won't be an easy task against one of the top-ranked defenses in the country in Tennessee . Entering the matchup with the Aggies, the Volunteers have 39 sacks, the most in all of college football and haven't allowed more than 27 points this season. On the flip side, quarterback Marcel Reed and his offense have scored at most 2 touchdowns against Power 4 opponents in the past month. To make matters worse, the Aggies became the first team in college football history to have over 450 yards, zero turnovers, and fail to score a touchdown in their latest loss to South Carolina. With those facts in mind, will the Maroon and White find a way to reverse their fortune, or will their matchup against the Volunteers be more of the same bland offense that has shown up for the better part of nine games? The two schools haven't met at Kyle Field in 10 years, when the Aggies won a wild double-overtime thriller, but let's see what the staff of Texas A&M Aggies on SI have to say about the outcome of this one. Staff Predictions for Tennessee at Texas A&M The Aggies’ offense is no match for Tennessee’s vaunted defense as Texas A&M fails to score a touchdown (again). Also, I seriously can’t believe the spread on this game. The gambling lords in the desert don’t understand vibes. Tennessee 21, A&M 6 The last time the Aggies hosted a conference opponent at Kyle Field, they were victorious over the Arkansas Razorbacks, one of the lower-tier teams in the SEC. Marcel Reed has shown improvement in his play over the past two games, but Tennessee’s defense is going to be his biggest test, and Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop will give A&M’s run defense a run for their money as well. But A&M’s run defense has shown their stinginess against prime running backs, and scoring in the red zone this year against A&M’s defense is an impressive feat to pull off. If they can keep that rolling against the Vols, then SEC win number two is well within range for the Maroon and White, especially if George MacIntyre is starting. A&M could be P.O.ed just enough to make that happen. A&M 28, Tennessee 24 It's hard to have confidence in the Aggies offense, and it's even tougher to believe in them going against one of the best defenses in the country. The Volunteers should take advantage of a team playing uninspired football and handle business. Tennessee 31, A&M 10 Kolton Becker A&M needs this game to avoid having to win the next two games to become bowl-eligible. Does that mean it can happen? We’ll find out more Saturday, but a lot of the numbers indicate that Tennessee’s defense and offense should be able to take care of business. I think that happens. Tennessee 38, A&M 30 Two great defenses, one miserable offense. But a blind squirrel finds a nut once in a while. Maybe with a cold breeze, this will be the time. picks.headline: Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M
picks.blurb: Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Dejounte Murray rants on socials Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: T.J. Searcy #18 of the Texas A&M Aggies reacts in the second half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jay Arnold · SB Nation Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas A&M returns to Kyle Field for the first time in three weeks after two straight road losses, sandwiched by an idle week. The Aggies fell 17-9 to South Carolina last time out in a contest that saw Texas A&M accumulate over 450 yards of offense and fail to produce a touchdown. The Aggies will hope to rectify that this week in College Station as they welcome the #8 Tennessee Volunteers to town. The trenches are going to be extremely important if Texas A&M is going to steal a win this Saturday. Let's dive into what needs to happen up front for the Aggies to come out on top. Offensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marcel Reed #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies runs with the ball in the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Against South Carolina, Texas A&M moved the ball well. As mentioned above, the Aggies racked up over 450 yards of offense. Rueben Owens ripped off multiple explosive runs, and Texas A&M had 206 yards on the ground. Yet, zero touchdowns made the hope that would be rendered by the yardage a grand disappointment instead. Simply put, field goals do not win games. The Aggies have to be able to finish drives off to win games, and Texas A&M has failed to do so in three out of the four road contests this season. The Texas A&M offense has fared better at home for the most part, but frankly I don't expect that to continue against an absolutely elite Tennessee defense. The Vols rank second only to Georgia in scoring defense. Tennessee's passing defense is staunch, though the Aggies wouldn't likely be able to test them there either. The rushing defense isn't in the upper tier of the conference but is also solid. Most significantly, the Volunteers lead the country in sacks. Defensive end Tyree Weathersby has seven sacks this season. The Vols also get pressure from the interior, as defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam has six sacks. Gilliam is a force to be reckoned with in the run game as well. I've thoroughly enjoyed watching film on the gifted DT this year, but I don't think his ability bodes well for this Texas A&M offensive line. I don't think this offensive line is horrible, and I think they've continued to play better as the season has progressed, but against this defensive front for Tennessee, it's going to feel like all that progress has left. In short, if the Aggies score a touchdown this week, I'd be surprised if it came from the offense. Defensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marco Jones #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies plays against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the situation for the offensive side of the ball is dire, I think the defensive side of the ball largely shouldered the burden well against South Carolina. The Aggies held what was the top rushing offense in the country at the time to under 100 yards right up until LaNorris Sellers ripped off a big run at the end. The Aggies also sacked Sellers twice, including a massive strip sack by Bryce Perry-Wright. We'll see if those run game improvements carry over as the Aggies face yet another powerful rushing attack. Powered by the legs of running back DeSean Bishop, Tennessee is the current top rushing attack in the SEC. However, if Texas A&M can find a way to slow down this rushing attack, the Aggies just might have a chance in this one. Discipline and sure tackling are going to be of the utmost importance as this Josh Heupel offense looks to spread opposing defenses out in order to capitalize on seams. Missed tackles against this Tennessee offense are extremely disastrous, and the Aggies can't afford to lose one-on-ones. The front four must maintain gap discipline as the secondary will be forced to honor Tennessee's formations. Get Tennessee behind the chains, and this becomes a drastically different ball game. While Tennessee ranks at the top of the conference in rushing, the Volunteers are the only team in the SEC below Texas A&M in passing offense. After Faizon Brandon started the season under center for Tennessee, George MacIntyre has since taken over. However, neither QB is a game changer on this offense, making the Vols basically one-dimensional. The equation for success against Tennessee is simple. Stop running backs DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris or get ground to a pulp. If the Aggies can make the improvements against the run permanent, they can hang around in this one – and that starts with the defensive tackle position and Brandon Davis-Swain, DJ Hicks, CJ Mims, and Landon Rink, in my opinion. While I think the Aggies keep this contest close in the first half, I think repeated three-and-outs by the Aggie offense eventually allow the Volunteers to wear down the Texas A&M defense in the second half. I have Tennessee winning this one 20-3. #BTHOtennessee

away.blurb: Camden Hall/Getty Images College Football The No. 8 Tennessee Volunteers will be without their second-leading rusher for some time. The school announced that running back Daune Morris suffered "non-life threatening injuries, including a broken leg" after a one-vehicle accident early Friday morning: A sophomore, Morris has rushed for 434 yards and three touchdowns on 66 carries this season, while also catching six passes for 35 yards. Morris played a significant role in the Vols' 34-6 drubbing of then-No. 6 Kentucky last weekend, rushing for 85 yards and a touchdown on just five carries. DeSean Bishop led the way on the ground for Tennessee, though, rushing for 109 yards and two scores. Bishop is the team's leading rusher this season with 1,066 yards and 13 touchdowns, and he figures to have an even bigger workload than usual on Saturday with Morris on the shelf. Meanwhile, Javin Gordon will likely operate as the RB2 after rushing for 129 yards and no touchdowns on 28 carries over five appearances this season. But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. USC vs. Indiana: Need to know Can USC match Indiana's physicality?: Regardless of who is at quarterback for Indiana, USC's defense will have its hands full with the Hoosiers' skill talent. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. A loss would leave the Hoosiers with a 66.8% chance of selection and bring greater scrutiny to a resume lacking high-end fare. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. The only exception was a 47-15 win against an overmatched Rutgers team. The Hoosiers haven't shown the ability to pull away and dominate quality opposition. So long as IU limits catastrophic turnovers, it will win the game on the basis of its physicality on both lines of scrimmage. But it's difficult to envision the Hoosiers suddenly pulling away from a team of USC's caliber. The Trojans have a veteran quarterback in Jayden Maiava who can keep his team in the game. away.blurb: Heading into Week 11 against USC, Indiana has several big names that are currently listed on the Big Ten availability report . Most notably, Turbo Richard, Kellan Wyatt, and Joe Brunner have already been ruled out. With Richard out, Lee Beebe Jr. figures to take on a leading role in the Hoosier backfield once again. Beebe stepped up in a big way when Richard was down with injury, and has been a reliable threat on the ground. In total, Beebe has 715 rushing yards to go along with 4 touchdowns on 134 attempts. Veteran OL Joe Brunner is also out. Brunner is a seasoned offensive lineman in his fifth season of college football, and has played a vital role on the Hoosier offensive line this season. He has started all nine games at right guard, and this is the first time he has popped up on the injury report. In his absence, freshman Sam Simpson could see more playing time, unless Cignetti switches things up and moves some names around. LB Rolijah Hardy is listed as questionable, and not having him on the field would be a tough loss for the Hoosiers against a dangerous USC offensive attack. Hardy is second on the team with 58 tackles this season. CB A.J. Harris is listed as probable. Harris has already missed time this season, and has appeared on the injury report several times. USC has a solid passing offense, so getting Harris in the mix would bode well for Indiana's chances of victory. After enjoying a much-needed bye week, the Indiana Hoosiers are set to take the field again in Week 11. Indiana hosts USC on Saturday afternoon in Bloomington in a game that could heavily impact the Big Ten race and College Football Playoff picture. The 4th-ranked Hoosiers find themselves as 8.5-point favorites over the 18th-ranked Trojans, but as we've seen before this season, Indiana has a habit of playing in close games. Looking for a decisive victory on its home turf, Indiana could be without some key playmakers. For the most part, the Hoosiers have stayed healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has an effective strategy in place to keep his team healthy, which includes managing practice workloads, prioritizing player recovery, and emphasizing proper nutrition and conditioning to minimize the risk of injuries. But no matter how effective that plan is, we are still talking about football here. Unfortunately, injuries are a regular sight. home.blurb: BLOOMINGTON — Barring a setback, Indiana football quarterback Josh Hoover looks like he will be available to start against USC. The No. 9 Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten) do have some other injury concerns going into a must-win game against the No. 18 Trojans (7-2, 4-2). They have four key contributors (three starters) on the report with leading rusher Turbo Richard and defensive end Kellan Wyatt already listed as out for Saturday's game. Indiana has been down at least one running back — Khobie Martin missed half the season with an arm injury — for much of the year. Martin made his return to the lineup against the Gophers, but he only has three carries for seven yards on the season. The Hoosiers also listed cornerback A.J. Harris and linebacker Rolijah Hardy as questionable. Hardy was a late scratch against Minnesota with a back injury while Harris hobbled off the field in the second half. Harris missed time earlier this season with a knee injury, but played well after regaining his spot in the starting lineup. Jaylen Bell, who stepped in for Harris earlier this season, would likely get the start if the Penn State transfer is ruled out. home.blurb: Heading into Week 11 against USC, Indiana has several big names that are currently listed on the Big Ten availability report . Most notably, Turbo Richard, Kellan Wyatt, and Joe Brunner have already been ruled out. With Richard out, Lee Beebe Jr. figures to take on a leading role in the Hoosier backfield once again. Beebe stepped up in a big way when Richard was down with injury, and has been a reliable threat on the ground. In total, Beebe has 715 rushing yards to go along with 4 touchdowns on 134 attempts. Veteran OL Joe Brunner is also out. Brunner is a seasoned offensive lineman in his fifth season of college football, and has played a vital role on the Hoosier offensive line this season. He has started all nine games at right guard, and this is the first time he has popped up on the injury report. In his absence, freshman Sam Simpson could see more playing time, unless Cignetti switches things up and moves some names around. LB Rolijah Hardy is listed as questionable, and not having him on the field would be a tough loss for the Hoosiers against a dangerous USC offensive attack. Hardy is second on the team with 58 tackles this season. CB A.J. Harris is listed as probable. Harris has already missed time this season, and has appeared on the injury report several times. USC has a solid passing offense, so getting Harris in the mix would bode well for Indiana's chances of victory. After enjoying a much-needed bye week, the Indiana Hoosiers are set to take the field again in Week 11. Indiana hosts USC on Saturday afternoon in Bloomington in a game that could heavily impact the Big Ten race and College Football Playoff picture. The 4th-ranked Hoosiers find themselves as 8.5-point favorites over the 18th-ranked Trojans, but as we've seen before this season, Indiana has a habit of playing in close games. Looking for a decisive victory on its home turf, Indiana could be without some key playmakers. For the most part, the Hoosiers have stayed healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has an effective strategy in place to keep his team healthy, which includes managing practice workloads, prioritizing player recovery, and emphasizing proper nutrition and conditioning to minimize the risk of injuries. But no matter how effective that plan is, we are still talking about football here. Unfortunately, injuries are a regular sight. In this week's Roundtable, Maize n Brew staff members give some takeaways from last week's game against MSU, some bold predictions for tomorrow's game and more! As always, let's reflect on last week's game. Provide any takeaways you had from the MSU game. Von : My takeaway is that this coaching staff should consider themselves lucky to still have jobs here. If it weren't for Warde Manuel resigning at the end of the year, as well as the university waiting for the president to begin her term next month, Kyle Whittingham may have been the one fired, not just Jason Beck. That game last weekend was as embarrassing a loss as I remember my time being on this planet, and that includes the dreaded 2020 season, App State, and everything to do with Rich Rod and Brady Hoke. It was truly that bad. Matt : It's over. Any shred of hope we had about the Whittingham era is now gone. To be incapable of scoring points on THAT Michigan State defense missing half its starters until garbage time is unacceptable. To then throw the players under the bus in the postgame press conference is an abomination. When futility stats that have existed for 90+ years are being broken, action has to be taken. Grace : Yikes! What a rough watch. It's disappointing and I feel for guys that have stuck with Michigan. Rod Moore, Zeke Berry and Jyaire Hill come to mind. While Kyle Whittingham doesn't seem to understand what this school is about, I think those guys do and this is just a terrible way for this season to continue. Scotty : My biggest takeaway is that we have officially hit rock bottom. What an embarrassing loss. Draw a line in the sand — do you want this coaching staff back next year? If you would keep some coaches but make changes, explain what you would do. Von : The only one I would entertain coming back is Jay Hill — he has been Harry Houdini in a season otherwise devoid of magic. So yes, I'd try and keep Hill around, but if the only way to guarantee Whittingham isn't back next year is if Hill can't come back, I'd be completely fine with it. I would do my best to hire away Bob Chesney from UCLA, knowing that is unlikely to happen. If he says no, open up the search even more and hope to God someone better is out there. Kellen : I'd keep Jay Hill, but everyone else can go. It took Whittingham too long to care to make a change like he did on Sunday. There's no sense of urgency. Matt : I would love to keep Jay Hill and some of the defensive staff. However, I want Whittingham and the entire offensive staff gone so badly that I would be willing to sacrifice the entire staff in order to start over. Even if the offense does get better under interim coordinator Jim Harding, Whittingham cannot be back under any circumstances or else the program will fall even further into disarray. Nick : Jay Hill and anyone he wants to keep from the defensive staff should be the only coaches that stick around next year. Kyle Whittingham clearly is asleep at the wheel and isn't the man for the job that we thought he would be when he was first hired. Despite all the drama and bad play that this season has brought, Hill and his side of the ball have been total pros about everything, and I think that's something you can't let get away. Whether it be making him the next head coach permanently or giving him all the money in the world to stick around with a new head coach, I think the school has to consider doing whatever it takes to keep him in town. Grace : No. I don't. I understand if it doesn't happen, but the way Whittingham is already talking about 2027 recruits and the transfer portal as solutions is just a way of saying "I'm not the problem, it's the players." With Ohio State left on the schedule and some of these guys nearing the end of the careers, I think that's a bad look. Scotty : I would love Jay Hill to stick around. I'm iffy on some others, but Kyle Whittingham cannot be this team's coach next year. Oregon…do we even care about the game at this point? Are we at the point of apathy, or are we still fully engaged hoping this team makes a bowl game? Von : I'm rooting for the players to succeed, but man, these next three weeks can't go by fast enough. Kellen : I'm excited to see if the men's basketball team can bounce back from the UConn loss. That's a high quality opponent and a good test for the Wolverines. That's two games in a row against elite opponents (the first being Houston) that we haven't seen them look great against elite opponents. As for the women's team, the UConn win is up there as the best win in program history. That team has a legit chance at a national title run, has at least four WNBA players, and there's a non-zero chance that we're getting a KBA statue outside of Crisler before 2060. Does that answer your questions? Matt : Hello darkness, my old friend. Apathy has arrived in its purest form. Who cares about a bowl game anymore? You could have said 10 years ago that making a bowl game was great because it allowed for an extra month of practice and a chance to see a team play one more time. This year, making a bowl game is futile because a majority of these players will be somewhere else next year anyways. I would be somewhat surprised if Michigan could even field a team for the bowl game given the amount of players that are sure to opt out and enter the portal the day after the Ohio State game. Nick : I don't think there's any way Michigan wins this week with Oregon seemingly finding itself again. This might not be the best Oregon team we've seen in recent years, but it is still capable of handling business, especially against a Michigan team that's totally lost right now. As for the rest of the year, I think UCLA is a lost cause as well. I won't rule out anything with the Ohio State game with the Buckeyes' season falling off a cliff. I did watch that 2024 game with my own two eyes, too. I even went back to watch the highlights a few times to verify that Michigan did win, so nothing would surprise me on that front. Regardless of how things pan out the rest of the way though, Michigan's 2026 season is over and the program needs to wipe the slate clean for 2027. Grace : Every week I'll be hoping for the improbable. I'm rooting for the players, but I'm not enthusiastic or optimistic. Scotty : This is a weird one for me. Obviously I can never root against Michigan, but I can't stand to see Whit come back for another year. The season is over, and missing a bowl feels like the best bet to make sure he's gone. I'll be cheering for Michigan as always, but I won't care or be upset when the game ends with a loss. Give us a bold prediction for tomorrow's game. Von : The game is scoreless after the first quarter, but the Ducks outscore the Wolverines by at least four touchdowns the rest of the game. Kellen : Michigan scores the first touchdown of the game and then doesn't score again. Matt : Michigan rushes for negative yardage on the game. Nick : I think Bryce Underwood plays a significant amount of snaps. Tommy Carr looked pretty rough throwing the ball against Michigan State and the Ducks could eat him alive, especially behind an offensive line that's in utter shambles. Carr will get the start at least, but I don't think it'll last very long. Grace : Michigan doesn't get thumped. Scotty : Michigan gets shutout. What's the final score and why? picks.headline: Michigan at No. 16 Oregon College Football Preview
picks.blurb: Michigan at No. 16 Oregon College Football Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Dejounte Murray rants on socials Michigan at No. 16 Oregon College Football Preview Kyle Yost · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Everything is bad! Maybe a (long overdue) change at offensive coordinator will help a little, but the dead cat bounce at quarterback lasted exactly two quarters. Now even that switch seems up in the air, as the Michigan Wolverines try to somehow get to bowl eligibility, which actually is far from guaranteed with three tough games remaining. First among those is a date with the Oregon Ducks, who shockingly already have three losses — and a lost quarterback — yet are somehow back in the playoff hunt. Like Kyle Whittingham, Dan Lanning has also made a change at coordinator, and back-to-back ranked wins have the Ducks well positioned for a 9-3 finish with a real shot at the CFP, and even the (final!) Big Ten Championship Game. Vibes are pretty lopsided heading into Saturday, and this would not be the first time Michigan has faced Oregon after a humiliating defeat. That 2007 contest did not go super well, and the 2026 edition is likely to repeat history, but at this point who knows anything. Frustration has turned to apathy in Ann Arbor, so this weekend really only has upside…right? Michigan (5-4, 2-4) at No. 16 Oregon (6-3, 4-2) Date & Time : Saturday, Nov. 14, 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR TV/Streaming : FS1 These teams have met once already as conference foes, with the then-No. 1 Ducks earning the win at the Big House over a 5-3 Michigan team that looked pretty rough under Sherrone Moore and Wink Martindale. Davis Warren only threw for 165 yards that game but posted 7.2 YPA and two touchdowns. At best, this program is no better off than it was 24 months ago, and arguably is in worse shape now. Offense: Deck chairs Week after week this offense finds new ways to disappoint, but last Saturday really felt like rock bottom. There were no redeeming qualities from the debacle against State, aside from finally breaking the camel's back, and while the removal of Jason Beck likely helps, how much it will actually improve the No. 126-ranked scoring offense is up for debate. The Ducks are middle of the pack in points per game and yards per game, and are equally effective against the run and pass. Losing edge Teitum Tuioti is a tough blow, but this defense should still be ok against Michigan without him. Objectively, Oregon's defense has taken a step back this season, but it might be hitting its stride at the right time. If the Wolverines struggle to move the ball, it is quite possible Bryce Underwood gets some snaps. To the surprise of no one, the lights have been too bright for Tommy Carr, and the downside of Underwood is no worse than his successor's. The lingering reason for hope is the run game, as Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter are far too good to be putting up such awful numbers. Beck is gone, and hopefully is the rhino; better play calling is a must. Defense: Do your job Whittingham's only pathway for the rest of the season is turning every game into the 2024 Ohio State win that sees the defense do enough to pull off the low-scoring upset. Even with some annoying moments last weekend, this unit is capable of doing just that. The pressure is immense knowing how much burden it must carry for the offense, but SP+ still considers this a top-three defense. Oregon replaced an injured Dante Moore with Dylan Raiola, who has been pretty solid thus far with 11 touchdowns to just two interceptions and a 65-percent completion rate on 7.3 YPA. He lit up Northwestern and did well against Ohio State, getting the ball to stud receiver Dakorien Moore. The Ducks are definitely a tricky offense to go against, especially when they feel confident in the passing game. However, the run game has been much less impressive, in part due to a bad offensive line. Jay Hill will have a chance to overwhelm up front and make Raiola uncomfortable, trusting the secondary to lock up receivers long enough to stall out drives. One thing to watch is fumbles, as Oregon has the second-most losses (10) in the country this season, though that is skewed by the bizarre afternoon against UCLA. Michigan needs one more win. Before the season started, this weekend was arguably the most obvious loss, then Oregon started looking bad and there was a glimmer of optimism, but since then the teams have gone in opposite directions. With red-hot UCLA up next, is the best chance for victory somehow in Columbus? What even is this season. I do not expect the Wolverines to win on Saturday, even with Beck gone and Underwood potentially back in. That is unfortunate, as this Oregon team is seemingly as vulnerable as it ever will be, and the Michigan defense has a chance to play fairly evenly on that side of the ball. The same cannot be said for the ground attack, though, which will not take advantage of the Ducks' front seven like Oklahoma State and Northwestern did. That leaves us in a weird place where I do not think a blowout is the most likely outcome, but neither is an upset. Oregon has done enough to save its season, while Whittingham has essentially done the opposite, more likely to lose his job after every week. Even a minor resurgence on offense could be enough for a favorable result, but that would be a pretty big surprise.

home.headline: Oregon's Teitum Tuioti exits Ohio State game with injury. What we know
home.blurb: Coach Dan Lanning said Nov. 9 Tuioti will be out for the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 263-pound senior out of Sheldon High School is the Ducks' third-leading tackler this season with 44. He also has a team-high 9.0 TFLs and eight quarterback hits. His 5.5 sacks are second on the team. Tuioti's injury came on a fourth-and-13 pass rush with 9:16 to play as his leg buckled when he was attempting to spin out of a block. COLUMBUS, Ohio – Oregon pulled off the upset Nov. 7 with a 41-28 win against Ohio State. But the victory came with a costly injury for the Ducks . Starting outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti injured his knee in the fourth quarter and was wearing a wrap as he was carted to the locker room after the game ended. "Unfortunately, Teitum's done for the year," Lanning said. "He had a knee injury, he'll end up having surgery. He's going to have to wait a little bit for things to settle down. I hate it for him, because it's kind of a routine, weird play that it happened on." In 51 career games, Tuioti has 200 tackles, 36.5 TFLs and 22.5 sacks. He was a three-year starter who does have one more season of eligibility remaining at Oregon, though a he also projected to be a Day 2 NFL Draft pick. "I don't know if he'll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is going to be really really lucky," Lanning said. "Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year and every year that he's been here. Watching him grow as a player and as a person has been really fun for us." Teitum Tuioti injury: How it happened He was down on the field for a few minutes and needed help getting to the sideline. Tuioti had two tackles in the game, including one for a loss of yards. He also played a key role in one of the Ducks' most impactful plays when he took a direct snap with Oregon in punt formation and threw a 30-yard pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei for a first down. For Oklahoma, it won’t mean much in terms of a playoff push, but it will go a long way in salvaging what’s been a lost season. The Sooners don’t have consecutive wins (or losses) on the season yet, but they have collected wins over Texas and Florida in the last five weeks. For Ole Miss, its CFP hopes are on thin ice and to even be somewhat involved in the conversation next month, the Rebels badly need to win their final three regular season games. Ole Miss initially opened as a 2.5-point road favorite last week, but will now enter the weekend as a narrow 1.5-point underdog. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss On SI Staff Predictions Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) runs beside Ole Miss Rebels linebacker Suntarine Perkins (4) during a college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the Ole Miss Rebels at Gaylord Family Ð Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. Ole Miss won 34-26. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis This weekend will mark another notable challenge for Ole Miss on the offensive side of the ball. It’s not an ideal weekend to not have Patrick Kutas available either, arguably Ole Miss’ top offensive lineman over the past two seasons. Oklahoma brings a defensive front that’s up to nearly 30 sacks on the year and one of the best run defenses in the conference, entering game day. Ole Miss desperately needs to bounce back in both departments, as it surrendered five sacks and ran for just 66 rushing yards in its loss last week. While there’s no doubt Ole Miss’ offensive line will get tested, and that Oklahoma will be sending consistent pressure, I’m picking Trinidad Chambliss to capitalize on what is looking like his final test against a great collegiate defense. Though Ole Miss will be without its leading tackler in Keaton Thomas, Oklahoma’s offense shouldn’t pose much of a threat anyway. It’s a golden opportunity for the Rebels to get right on that side of the ball. I expect a close game in Norman, thanks to the Sooners’ defense, but if one team was going to separate itself by multiple scores I think it would likely be Oklahoma. Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 20 Matt Galatzan Ole Miss needs to get back on track if it is going to save its season. Fortunately, Oklahoma is the perfect opponent to do just that. The Sooners have struggled mightily this season, and the Rebels have the best quarterback in the country, and their backs against the wall. I think Ole Miss wins, and wins big. Billy Flowers I can see this matchup going one of two ways: Ole Miss comes out of the week angry and inspired and beats the brakes off Oklahoma, or Oklahoma coach Brent Venables exploits the weaknesses the Rebels showed against Georgia, and the game is close. Unfortunately, I see the latter as more likely. I think Ole Miss' offense comes out flat, and the grocery list of injuries bites the Rebels in the back. I don't think the Rebel defense is strong enough to shut down Oklahoma's offense completely. I expect Oklahoma to weasel out a tight one. Oklahoma 23, Ole Miss 20 Coming off such an embarrassing loss to Georgia, I think Ole Miss bounces back this weekend against Oklahoma. I don’t think either team’s offense will be particularly strong on Saturday. However, I have more faith in Ole Miss’ offense to recover from a string of poor performances, even if Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is out and Jason Witten has taken over as the Sooners’ interim offensive coordinator and play-caller. Give me the Rebels by three points in a game defined by the two teams’ defenses. Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 24 Cooper Ferguson Ole Miss is in desperate need of a bounce-back performance after getting embarrassed by Georgia last weekend. The Rebels have plenty of questions to answer offensively, especially with Kewan Lacy and Patrick Kutas out. Oklahoma’s defense is one of the toughest units in the SEC, and I expect Brent Venables to make life difficult for Trinidad Chambliss throughout the afternoon. However, I still have faith in Pete Golding’s defense to get the job done against an Oklahoma offense that is still trying to find its identity under Jason Witten. The Sooners looked better against Florida, but I need to see more before buying into the offensive turnaround. Ole Miss has too much at stake to let another opportunity slip away, and I expect Chambliss to lead a late scoring drive to secure a critical road victory. Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 20 For Ole Miss, it comes down to scoring on the Sooners. Oklahoma lacks a sufficient run game, and at times, John Mateer can really struggle. If the Rebels lose, it will likely be because of that deadly defense. I predict that the Sooners defend their home territory and win 21-17 with a great defensive performance. I hope the Rebels prove me wrong, but they need to improve a lot, including their run game and tackling. The defense looks better, but the offense doesn’t do quite enough to defeat Oklahoma. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. Oklahoma is 0-3 all-time in the series but is coming off of one of its most complete games of the season in their win over the Florida Gators . The offense found a rhythm and consistency we haven't seen much this year, and the defense suffocated the Florida Gators, holding them to seven points and forcing two interceptions. This week, with the Rebels coming to town, the Sooners face a much different challenge. Ole Miss boasts one of the most dynamic quarterbacks in college football, in Trinidad Chambliss. Chambliss is 15th in the nation in passing yards and second in the SEC behind LSU's Sam Leavitt. He's a threat to make plays with his legs as well, as we saw last year in the Rebels' win in Norman. On a slippery Owen Field, Chambliss threw for 315 yards and ran for 53 yards in Ole Miss's 34-26 win over Oklahoma. The Sooners defense will need to do a better job containing Chambliss if they want to win this Saturday and earn bowl eligibility. Can Oklahoma find a way to earn back-to-back victories for the first time since the LSU and Missouri wins at the end of last season? Here's how our staff at Sooners Wire sees the game playing out. Sooners Defense Leads to Win Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Oklahoma Sooners defensive back Peyton Bowen (22) runs to score a touchdown against the Texas Longhorns during the second half at Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images It'll be a battle between two defense-minded coaches, and the Sooners are still riding high with Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten at the helm, while Ole Miss' offense is sputtering thanks to key injuries to its offensive line, star running back, and possibly the quarterback. For one of the few times this season, the injury report looks to be in favor of Oklahoma, which is looking to build on a win for the first time this season. With everyone theoretically healthy, one of the advantages Oklahoma has is that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss has become turnover-prone, throwing nine interceptions this season, while OU's defense does well at forcing those turnovers, coming in at No. 4 in the conference. It's no secret that the Sooners are typically successful when they win the turnover battle, and I think that will play a role in this one. It'll be a defensive battle, but OU will have the edge at home. Oklahoma 17, Ole Miss 14 James D. Jackson, Contributor Ole Miss Responds This season, Oklahoma has typically followed up an encouraging step forward with a discouraging step back, ever since the Texas game. Ole Miss is reeling after last week's loss to Georgia, and Brent Venables typically doesn't have his team as on point when the opponent is more desperate and hungry than the Sooners are. Things will probably slip after last week's upset win; there's too much of a pattern to think otherwise. If Trinidad Chambliss plays like he's capable of, Ole Miss wins. If OU recaptures some of the magic of last November, when the Sooners played consistent football, they can put an end to Ole Miss' teetering playoff hopes. Ole Miss 20, Oklahoma 17 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Ole Miss has the Better QB Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) drops back to pass during the fourth quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The Oklahoma Sooners continued their uneven play this season with a win over the Florida Gators. The Sooners have yet to win or lose back-to-back games this season. While it looked much better offensively under Jason Witten, the question is whether that will continue against the Ole Miss Rebels. This game is a true toss-up, but I've got to go with the quarterback I trust more and that's Trinidad Chambliss. Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 17 Jaron Spor, Contributor Offense Does it Again Nov 7, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws the ball during the first half against the Florida Gators at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images The Oklahoma offense took a positive step in the right direction last week with their road win over Florida. They found a way to win with a ball-control style that helped the Sooners win the time-of-possession battle by 15 minutes. The Sooners scored on three of their first four drives, laying the groundwork for what could be the plan to keep Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels' offense at bay this weekend. Ole Miss allows 394.7 yards per game, which is 15th in the SEC and 104th in the nation. This could be another opportunity for the Sooners' offense to take a big step forward. Ole Miss won 34-26. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis · Ole Miss Rebels On SI Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:30 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Ole Miss is looking to regroup in Norman against Oklahoma and needs to win out in order to possibly contend for a spot in the College Football Playoffs. The Rebels fell nine spots in this week's CFP rankings, following its uncompetitive loss to Georgia, and no longer possess control of their postseason destiny. Ole Miss On SI's Tyler Komis and co-host Bailey Flanders dive into Ole Miss' season up to this point and preview its game against Oklahoma this weekend. The two also discuss how realistic the program's path back to the CFP is this season in episode 111 of The Rebel Rundown . What Golding said about Oklahoma Oct 17, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on before the game against the Missouri Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "I think the defensive concepts of both defensive head coaches as well - it's like, 'okay, how do I shrink the game, number one, when you're playing an explosive offense?' That's by controlling the football, being able to establish the run game, which both those guys believe in. I think being defensive guys, you know what creates issues on defense alternative formations," Golding said. "I think you saw that with Florida. Last week there's ten snaps of unbalance plus one run game. I think they're getting the quarterback going in the run game as well to make you account for all 11. And then from a defensive standpoint create negative yardage plays (and are) very aggressive. Venables' defense is very much like you saw on Saturday (against Georgia). You know that was probably one of their higher pressure games being Georgia. You know a lot of seven up looks and things like that." "I think some of the post-snap RPO game has been eliminated a little bit. Some of that decision making process for the quarterback. They still have RPOs. I think a lot of them are pre-snap box generated based on numbers and free access and things like that. I think a lot of the run schemes are similar in the same way. I think they're trying to get the quarterback's legs going a little more than before. They've always had some quarterback designed runs, but it felt like that was more of an emphasis in the Florida game. Obviously (Jason) Witten being a tight end, the tight end's going to be a piece of the package, and they've got some good tight ends," Golding said of Oklahoma's new interim offensive coordinator. "You know 81 is a really good player. But I think taking more off the quarterback you know as far as from a progression standpoint and reads post-snap and being a little more specific in the run game based on formation. A little more alternative with a shift and a motion, which has kind of been the theme against us anyway. So I think simplifying it within reason and then making you account for the quarterback." away.headline: Ole Miss injury report got shorter in one place and more concerning in another
away.blurb: No. 19 Ole Miss' side of the Student-Athlete Availability Report got cleaned up in Thursday night's update. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and wide receiver Deuce Alexander were removed from the report. Both were listed as probable in the initial report Wednesday. Their availability for Saturday was never in much doubt. The same can't be said for the three Rebels listed as questionable, including one new addition. Running back Makhi Frazier was added to the report Thursday, joining defensive end Kam Franklin and safety Sharif Denson under the questionable designation. Frazier's addition is particularly concerning considering the Rebels are already without star running back Kewan Lacy, who has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury. Without Lacy, Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight have been responsible for much of the workload in the Rebels' backfield. If Frazier can't play Saturday, Mills-Knight could be asked to take on an even larger role against the Sooners. Ole Miss is also dealing with significant injuries elsewhere on the roster. Starting right guard Patrick Kutas and linebacker Keaton Thomas are among the 11 Rebels ruled out for Saturday's game. Franklin and Denson, meanwhile, remain uncertain after appearing on both availability reports this week. The next update is scheduled for Friday night, with final designations coming before Saturday's kickoff in Norman. The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. More news : Brian Kelly Sends Blunt Warning to Texas Ahead of LSU Clash Lacy quickly emerged as one of the best players in college football last season, rushing for 1,567 yards (third most in FBS) and 24 touchdowns (second) on an FBS-leading 306 attempts, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, along with 177 receiving yards. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. His third, and potentially final, college season ends after just six games, finishing with 388 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 78 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Makhi Frazier, a Junior transfer from Michigan State, and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight will continue to handle the bulk of the carries for Ole Miss. Frazier has 365 rushing yards on 72 carries this season (5.1 yards per carry), while Mills-Knight has 165 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries (5.0 yards per carry). away.headline: Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. home.headline: Ole Miss Announces Trinidad Chambliss Injury Before Oklahoma Showdown
home.blurb: Ole Miss listed Chambliss as probable for Saturday in the initial SEC availability report , putting the Rebels' starting quarterback on track to play. However, the Rebels didn't detail the injury, and Chambliss didn't show issues in last weekend's game. That makes Chambliss' probable designation significant for an Ole Miss team attempting to recover from its worst offensive performance of the season. The Rebels managed only seven points in Saturday's 42-7 loss to Georgia, falling to 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play. Ole Miss Announces Trinidad Chambliss Injury Before Oklahoma Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Dejounte Murray rants on socials Ole Miss Announces Trinidad Chambliss Injury Before Oklahoma Showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Ole Miss Rebels announced unforeseen news on quarterback Trinidad Chambliss as the program prepares for a crucial road matchup against the Oklahoma Sooners. Depending on Chambliss' status, the Rebels could fall off of the College Football Playoff run entirely — they are ranked No. 19 in the latest CFP rankings — and put an early, virtual end to their season. Chambliss completed 18 of 34 passes for 170 yards against the Bulldogs but failed to score a touchdown for the first time this season. He also threw an interception as Georgia controlled the game throughout. Through Week 10, Chambliss has completed 207 of 330 passes for 2,359 yards, 18 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He has added 187 rushing yards and seven touchdowns on 57 carries. Although this news is upsetting for Chambliss, he made up for it by landing national recognition earlier this week. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6).Ayrton Breckenridge/Clarion Ledger / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Ole Miss announced Tuesday that Chambliss is one of 18 semifinalists for the Maxwell Award. Meanwhile, Chambliss has also moved into seventh place on the program's career passing-yardage list and eighth with 40 career touchdown passes. The Rebels' No. 19 ranking heading into Saturday's matchup leaves little room for another defeat, even though Chambliss' expected appearance should boost their chances of getting a win. Ole Miss visits Oklahoma on Saturday at 4:15 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Jon Sumrall returns to Kroger Field in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 6:15 p.m. ET (ESPN) when his Florida program takes on his alma mater, Kentucky. The Wildcats are 3.5-point home favorites, and my Florida vs. Kentucky prediction and college football picks expect Will Stein's team to win this game in the trenches. Who will win Florida vs Kentucky: Kentucky -3.5 After a hot September that had Florida ranked in the top 10 and climbing the college football national championship odds , the Gators have been one of the worst teams in the SEC. Since upsetting Ole Miss, Florida is 1-4 straight-up and against the spread, and their struggles will continue against Jon Sumrall's alma mater. I would take Kentucky to cover up to -4.5 . Florida is coming off its worst loss of the season, losing 23-17 at home to Oklahoma as a 3.5-point favorite, and switching back to Aaron Philo at QB won't save a team that's averaging 15.6 points per game since the start of October. The last time we saw Philo, he was benched in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party. Kentucky's defense isn't Georgia's, but it is disruptive enough to slow Florida down. The Wildcats rank 21st nationally in havoc rate (18.9%) and seventh in interceptions (12). TOP PICK Florida vs Kentucky Over/Under pick: Over 52.5 Florida's defense has been the death of it all season, and it hit an all-time low last week, making John Mateer look good. Kentucky's offense is far more efficient, and the reason I'd play the Over at 52.5 or better. The Wildcats have one of the best offensive lines in the country, paving the way for a unit ranked 16th nationally in success rate (49.2%) . With Kenny Minchey's efficiency (77.8% adjusted completion percentage) and the Wildcats' advantage on the line, they shouldn't have trouble converting on money downs against a defense sitting 132nd in third/fourth down success rate (54.8%). However, the Gators will move the ball too against a Kentucky defense that struggles to stop the run. The Wildcats are currently 96th in defensive success rate (45.8%), and Florida running back Jadan Baugh ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles (48). Florida vs Kentucky combo During Florida's skid, its biggest issue has been slow starts. In its five games since the start of October, the Gators have trailed by 6+ points at halftime in each. Florida won and covered in just one of those games. If that trend continues, Kentucky should pull away in the second half, especially with Florida's defensive issues. Earlier in the season, the Gators could make up for the fact that their defense has one of the worst secondaries in the country, but since losing top wide receiver Vernell Brown III , they haven't been the same. The sophomore was averaging 3.87 yards per route run with zero drops; Florida's other starting receivers each have a drop rate of at least 7.7%. Brown hasn't played since the upset win over Ole Miss and is once again listed out on the SEC injury report .
