picks.blurb: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Dejounte Murray rants on socials Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will Stein's Kentucky football team hosts Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators team under the lights at Kroger Field tomorrow at 6:15 P.M. ET. Florida has came back down to earth after a strong September and Kentucky is looking to bounce back after suffering their second loss of the season. We preview the Gators offense and defense, as well as laid out the path to victory for the Wildcats. Now, I will give my final thoughts on the matchup and a prediction for the game. Coach Stein said that last week was only the second time in his coaching career that his offense failed to score a touchdown. This team and the offense specifically will be looking to make a statement tomorrow night. They will get a perfect opportunity against a Brad White defense that has struggled all season for the Gators. As we know from watching years of Brad White's scheme in Lexington, they love to play soft zone coverage and allow easy completions to offenses in hopes of executing a bend-don't-break style of defense. The big advantage is this Kentucky offense is built off of efficiency and getting Kenny Minchey easy completions in quick game. This creates an advantageous scheme matchup for Will Stein and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. If the Wildcats can eliminate the self-inflicted mistakes from last week in Knoxville, you have to like their chances to put together long scoring drives. The difference in this game being close and the Cats running away with it is if the offense can start to find the explosive plays. One area of this matchup we have not talked about is the weather aspect of this football game on Saturday. The past few days in Lexington have turned extremely cold, and temperatures for kickoff at looking at 40 degrees or below. Combine that with the winds, it will be freezing at Kroger Field and will only get colder as the game goes on. You have to wonder how this Florida team will respond in these conditions especially if they don't start fast in this one. This Florida team is reeling, they have lost four of their last five games. The drop-off has been eye-opening for the Gators because they looked like one of the best teams in the country through the first month of the season. Defenses have figured out how to bottle up their run game and the offense has started to suffer because of it. The Gators offense led them to their hot start to the Jon Sumrall era and covered up the rough play on the defensive side of the football. Kentucky has to stop this rushing attack and get Florida into a dropback heavy game. The Gators are going back to Aaron Philo after starting Tramell Jones last week. The old saying goes: if you have two quarterbacks, you have none. I think the Wildcats will be prepared to potentially see both guys this week as the Gators will try everything they can to generate some offense. Florida has to answer questions offensively, their offensive line is one of the worst in the conference and the quarterback situation is not ideal. Brad White has not figured out how to fix the Gators defensive issues in his first year away from Lexington. I think Kentucky capitalizes on that and has one of their best offensive performances of the season following last week where they failed to reach the end zone. Kentucky has their backs against the wall, they will make the College Football Playoff if they win the last three games and I believe the offense makes a statement in the cold at Kroger Field. Prediction: Kentucky 38, Florida 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction

picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Florida game glance, opening odds, and early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Dejounte Murray rants on socials Kentucky vs. Florida game glance, opening odds, and early prediction dholbrook · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 11:15 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Neither Kentucky nor Florida will feel good coming into this one. Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. But they'll both have to get over it quickly; the SEC comes at you fast. Florida will travel up to Kentucky for a November night game; the last time that happened was just last year. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their mind, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. The Gators have been held to under 10 points in back-to-back games while also playing a QB carousel. Trammel Jones started against the Sooners but was a dreadful 10-of-22 with 2 INTs. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone's guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Florida Gators Location: Kroger Field- Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 14th Time: 6:15 PM ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel Sportsbook has Kentucky favored by 3.5 points with an over/under of 51.5. ESPN win probability: ESPN FPI gives Kentucky a 54% chance of victory Our prediction I'm not going to lie, this game has got weirdness written all over it. Kentucky and Florida are both coming off terrible losses, with both fan bases hurting. Whichever team handles that the best will walk away with a victory here. I think if Kentucky can get back to playing clean football, they have the talent and home-field advantage to send the Gators back home with a loss. But Florida has a lot of talent, and if they are motivated, they can beat anyone, anywhere, as proven down in Austin when they knocked off Texas. My biggest concern remains Malachi Wood, who has been abused by speed guys this season. Emmanuel Oyebadejo is a 6'6, 300-pound nightmare who leads the Gators with 4.5 sacks. You better believe he is licking his chops to go against the right side of Kentucky's line, which struggled down in Knoxville. Ultimately, I think Kentucky does clean it up, and despite some pressure off the edge, the Cats knock off the Gators. Final score: Kentucky 33, Florida 21 Which team do you think bounces back best from a tough loss?

Their chances of sneaking into the College Football Playoff took a big hit when their six-game winning streak ended with a 34-6 loss last week at Tennessee. picks.headline: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh
picks.blurb: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Dejounte Murray rants on socials Story by Wildcats Wire Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 11, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football failed the first test of this important November stretch, losing 34-6 to Tennessee . The Wildcats have to get off the mat quickly as they host the Florida Gators on Saturday night at Kroger Field. This is a Florida team that is reeling as they have lost four of their last five games. We will preview both sides of the football for the Gators, but we will start with their offense which is led by their star running back. Running back Jadan Baugh is essentially the entire Gators offense, he is the engine that makes it go. Similar to what we said about Tennessee's DeSean Bishop, but the Gators have struggled recently to get this run game going. That is the main reason they have lost four of their last five games. When you look at the win/loss splits of Baugh's stat line, it tells the whole story of Florida's offense. In the Gators' five wins this season, Baugh has rushed for 691 yards on 108 attempts for 12 rushing touchdowns and is averaging over six yards per carry in those wins. He has averaged 138 rushing yards per game in those five wins. Conversely, in Florida's four losses this season, Baugh has rushed for 145 yards on 52 attempts for 2 rushing touchdowns and is averaging under three yards per carry. He is averaging just 36 rushing yards per game in those losses. Teams have started to key in on the run game and slow Baugh down recently, as most of his success came in the first month of the season. In September when the Gators were rolling, Baugh had 600 rushing yards on 83 attempts and 11 of his 14 rushing touchdowns came in the first month of the season. He was averaging 150 rushing yards per game and over seven yards per carry in the month of September. Since then, Baugh has just 236 rushing yards on 77 attempts, averaging just 47 rushing yards per game and three yards per carry. It is simple for Kentucky's defense, stop this rushing attack led by Baugh and you will be in a great position to win this football game. Florida has a quarterback issue, as they have flipped back and forth between Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones. Philo was efficient in the first month of the season, but he dealt with an injury that allowed Jones to start in a big win on the road against Texas. Philo returned against Georgia, but a couple of boneheaded mistakes sent him to the bench. Jones completed 22-of-35 pass attempts for 155 passing yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the win over the Longhorns. Against Georgia and Oklahoma, the Gators only scored a total of 15 points. In those two losses, Jones completed 28-of-47 passes for 305 passing yards and no touchdown passes to three interceptions. Jones has thrown just four touchdown passes on the season and five interceptions. Philo on the other hand, has completed 70% of his passes this season for 1,367 yards for nine passing touchdowns. Philo also has five interceptions on the season. The biggest issue has been the injury of wide receiver Vernell Brown, who has not played in a game since the win over Ole Miss in September. Florida is struggling to generate any offense outside of the run game. This matchup is simple for Kentucky, they just have to key in and stop the run game for the Gators. Force Florida into a dropback heavy game, which will lead to turnover opportunities. Regardless if they start Philo or Jones, both have been turnover prone this season and the Gators are -3 in the turnover margin which ranks 98th among FBS teams. Kentucky's defense has to get stops early and play with a lead quickly. This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh

home.headline: Final availability report: No. 13 Tennessee vs. No. 6 Kentucky
home.blurb: Head coach Josh Heupel’s team has remained pretty healthy since the early-season injury problems. In this week’s availability reports, the Vols listed no new names and look to have everyone available. Earlier in the week, Heupel was asked how managing a team in November is different than September, and if they are equipped for it. On Friday night’s report , Kentucky reported four players out: inside linebacker Antwan Smith, inside linebacker Justyn Hartley, defensive back Jaden Smith, and defensive back Grant Grayton. Antwan Smith, Jaden Smith, and Grant Grayton have been out for quite some time. Outside linebacker Sam Greene and defensive back Isaiah McMillian were listed as probable. McMillian was initially questionable on Wednesday night but made progress. They are both removed from Saturday's report and available. Xavier Gilliam tunes out the hype as No. 13 Tennessee prepares for No. 6 Kentucky No. 13 Tennessee and No. 6 Kentucky will kick off at 6:20 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium. The Vols lead the all-time series with 86 wins, 26 losses and 9 ties, and carry a five-game win streak against the Wildcats into Saturday night. “I think you’re constantly trying to improve," Heupel said. "You’ve heard me say it, good teams continue to get better every part of the season. Every week’s its own season, too. And so you’ve got to be great in your preparation, how you practice, put yourself in a position to play smart football. Certainly as you go through the year, injuries, where you’re at, all those things, you have to manage it really week by week. Tends to be more towards the end of the season. But for us this year, we had a bunch of injuries early in the year.” Ninety minutes prior to kickoff, the Southeastern Conference released the final availability report for both teams, which is listed below. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The Wildcats will try to spoil the Utes' perfect season in a ranked battle Big 12 battle Getty Images Utah's trip to Arizona in Week 11 wasn't circled on many schedules before the 2026 college football season began, but the Big 12 matchup is a showdown between ranked teams and has serious College Football Playoff implications . The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. Getting to the Big 12 Championship isn't out of the question, but losses to BYU and Texas Tech make that hard. However, take down the unbeaten and No. 2 team, and watch the Cats rocket up the rankings. Or , Utah could come up with a terrific ranked win on the road, and at 10-0, it would all but lock up a spot in the CFP. Utah vs Arizona: Quick Hits Arizona still has work to do after this, no matter what, with a trip to Kansas State before hosting the Territorial Cup rivalry game against Arizona State. Utah has a sneaky-tough date at TCU after this before finishing with a sneaky-nasty game against a high-powered West Virginia. Arizona won the last meeting 23-10 in 2024, but Utah is 6-2 in the last eight meetings. Why Utah Will Win The Utes have been a machine when it comes to controlling the tempo and the time. They're great on third downs on both sides of the ball, the pass defense holds up great when pushed – it'll bend, but doesn't break – and they always seem to have the ball. They can hit the deep shots and be explosive, but they're at their best when quarterback Devon Dampier and the running game go on long marches. Utah keeps the ball a Big 12-best 32:50 a game, but … Why Arizona Will Win Arizona can match the Utes when it comes to tempo. Utah is No. 1 in the conference in time of possession, but Arizona holds the ball for well over 32 minutes, quarterback Noah Fifita is great at hitting short-range third-down throws, and the defense is usually a killer against the run. This isn't necessarily a ball-hawking Wildcat defense, but it's been better at taking the ball away with six over the last four games. Utah has turned it over twice in each ofthe last five games. Utah vs Arizona Prediction, Betting Lines It's all about the Utah ground game and whether or not it will go off. Arizona is 6-0 when allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards, and that includes holding down Cincinnati – the Big 12's No. 2 ground game – and a decent Iowa State attack. Who did the Cats get gouged by? Texas Tech ripped off 320 yards, West Virginia ran for over 300, and BYU averaged close to five yards per carry – the Wildcats lost to the Red Raiders and Cougars. Utah runs well, and it'll get a few gashing runs, but it was held in check by Colorado in Boulder, and didn't run all that well against BYU last week. But here's Utah's biggest problem – the Arizona pass rush. Dampier can move and make plays, but he and the Utah backfield get hit behind the line too often. The other issue for the Utes is a lack of pass rush that should bother Fifita enough to matter in key moments late. Arizona will survive, helped by a +2 turnover margin. picks.blurb: Utah Utes expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 14, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: “The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team’s biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He’s allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He’s an extremely competitive coach, but he’s able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop.” Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? “Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It’s giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he’s been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn’t have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing.” Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? “Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah’s offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he’s really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does.” Arizona’s secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? “The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size.” How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona’s passing attack? “Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it’s likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him.” Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we’re seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? “The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people’s person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It’s not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it’s a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He’s also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it’s just complaining, though he’d listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team.” Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. “This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it’s far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year’s past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they’ve got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 .” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. away.headline: Utah Coach Morgan Scalley Drops Significant Wayshawn Parker Update
away.blurb: Star running back Wayshawn Parker was limited after an early injury, which greatly impacted Utah's ability to move the ball on the ground. And while the Utes persevered against the Cougars, concerns about the junior RB's status for Utah's upcoming road bout with the Arizona Wildcats abounded after the win. He continued to play in the game, but was limited to just two first-half carries before finishing with 36 yards on 14 attempts. That makes for an average of just 2.6 yards per rush for Parker, who didn't see the end zone against BYU, either. Through nine games, Parker has amassed 762 yards on the ground to go with nine rushing touchdowns. He has also posed a significant pass-catching threat out of the backfield, hauling in 29 receptions for 269 yards and four additional touchdowns. Ryan Aston Ryan Aston covers college football and NBA basketball for Heavy.com. Based out of Salt Lake City, Utah, he has worked for the Standard-Examiner and covered sports and entertainment niches at FanSided, Bleacher Report, Screen Rant and elsewhere. The Utes secured a 28-20 victory at Rice-Eccles Stadium on Saturday, improving to 9-0 on the campaign and inching closer to a potential College Football Playoff berth. However, Morgan Scalley's team didn't escape the contest unscathed. During his latest weekly press conference, though, Scalley provided an update on Parker's status that should allow Utes fans to rest easy heading into their team's next Big 12 battle. Play Utah Coach Morgan Scalley Says Wayshawn Parker Will Be Ready for Next Week Scalley addressed Parker's health situation while speaking to reporters on Monday, leaving little doubt that the Richmond, California product would be ready to go against Noah Fifita and the Wildcats. "This is a guy that is tough as nails and fought through stuff. He's gonna be fine for the next game," Scalley declared regarding his rushing leader. "That's not gonna be an issue." Parker, who already looked to be less than 100 percent during Utah's Oct. 31 road win over the Cincinnati Bearcats, was injured on the very first play against BYU on Saturday. After taking a handoff from quarterback Devon Dampier during the Utes' opening drive and gaining six yards, Parker limped back to the sidelines. Just over 24 hours after Utah's Holy War win, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported via X that Parker was contending with a heel issue. home.headline: Colorado Loses Two Defenders in Latest Injury Report Before Arizona State
home.blurb: The Colorado Buffaloes have had very few bounces go their way in terms of injuries this season, but they were hopeful that may change in Week 10. The Buffaloes had a few players who weren’t ruled out for the majority of the week, and although they were battling injuries, there was still some hope they may play against the Arizona State Sun Devils. However, Friday’s update was the bearer of bad news for Colorado fans. All but one of those players were ruled out, and the final member of that list’s status is still undetermined. Sean Kinney will make his third straight start at center for Colorado against Northwestern. | University of Colorado Athletics Thankfully for Colorado, the two members of the injury report who were listed as probable will play. Those two were cornerback Cree Thomas and Sean Kinney. Namely, Kinney has been an impact player for the entire season since winning Colorado’s starting center job. Backup Demetrius Hunter went down with a likely season-ending injury in Week 1, and Kinney hasn’t wavered in his increased snap count. Mitchell has been an anchor in the Buffaloes’ secondary, as he and fellow safety Randon Fontenette have been the most dependable part of that unit. As for Taufatofua, he’s been dealt a bad hand with injuries this season, as he missed Colorado’s first four games as well. But when he made his return against the then-No. 12 Texas Tech Red Raiders in Week 5, he was a solid contributor right away. He assisted Santana Hopper in creating pressure as a hybrid defensive lineman, and Hopper likely wouldn’t have had the game he did without him. There was also hope that Welch could return this week , but that was shut down with the week’s first injury report. In addition, Scudero, who played in the first two games of the season, still hasn't returned from the injury report. His chances of playing again this season continue to get slimmer by the week. But those unfortunate updates go to show the type of luck Colorado has had with injuries this season. Manuel is the lone player from the Buffs’ midweek injury reports who still has a chance to play against ASU. He was upgraded to questionable on Thursday, and that status remained on Friday’s report. The Longhorns have recovered from a few early miscues and jumped back into the SEC title race. The Longhorns have won three straight games, including a 34-20 win over No. 18 Missouri last week. LSU faced its biggest test of the season against No. 5 Alabama and faltered, losing 31-13. The Tigers were unable to find any offensive consistency in the loss, rushing for only 2.3 yards per carry as the Crimson Tide won in all three phases. Texas and LSU have only played 18 times in history, and not in Baton Rouge since 1953. The last time they played was in 2019, when legendary quarterback Joe Burrow threw a dramatic touchdown pass on third-and-17 to put the game away. On his Always College Football Week 11 preview , McElroy picked LSU to win 24-20 and called the Tigers’ pass rush against Texas’ protection “probably the most lopsided matchup on the board” on a slate with four games between ranked playoff teams. McElroy pointed to the quarterback’s patience as part of the problem. “He does hold the ball looking for the perfect throw, and behind that line, the perfect throw sometimes arrives after the defense arrives,” McElroy said. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, an Austin native who followed Kiffin from Ole Miss, is the player McElroy expects to attack a Texas line that has struggled with twists and stunts. The Longhorns also listed offensive lineman Trevor Goosby as out on their availability report for the Missouri game. Alabama’s fourth-quarter surge in Baton Rouge led Booger McFarland to declare the Crimson Tide a playoff lock , and Texas brings a defense built to repeat that formula. The Longhorns rank first nationally in adjusted defensive EPA per play, according to Game on Paper . “Texas’ defense is good enough to hold LSU to field goals, which is why I think this stays a fight,” McElroy said. LSU’s tempo is the Tigers’ counter. McElroy noted that LSU runs nearly 80 plays per game and said, “If LSU’s tempo has the Texas linebackers gassed by, say, the fourth quarter, then the best defense on the field stops being the best defense on the field.” What’s at stake in Baton Rouge? away.headline: LSU Could Get a Surprising Defensive Reinforcement Against Texas
away.blurb: LSU defensive end Gabriel Reliford could be nearing a return to the field after being removed from the SEC availability report ahead of the Tigers' matchup with Texas Saturday, at Tiger Stadium. Reliford was initially listed as probable on Wednesday's report after recovering from a torn ACL suffered during spring practice. His removal from Thursday's report is an encouraging development for LSU, which could get another option along its defensive front at an important point in the season. While Reliford's availability doesn't necessarily mean he will immediately become a major contributor, his potential return could provide some much-needed depth to the Tigers' defensive-line rotation. Reliford's Return Could Give LSU Another Defensive Option Reliford hasn't appeared in a game during the 2026 season after suffering the ACL injury in the spring. The redshirt sophomore was initially expected to miss the entire regular season, making his potential return against Texas a notable development. That means the defensive end has dealt with two significant injuries in consecutive seasons, making it difficult to expect him to immediately return to the level of production LSU may eventually need from him. For LSU, even a limited workload from Reliford could be valuable. Adding another defensive end to the rotation would give the Tigers another option to work into their defensive-front packages without necessarily requiring him to play an extensive number of snaps. The timing of Reliford's potential return is particularly important with Texas coming to Baton Rouge . The Longhorns present another difficult test for LSU, and having additional bodies available along the defensive front could help the Tigers manage their workload throughout the game. For LSU, the development is a positive one regardless of whether Reliford plays a handful of snaps or works his way into a larger role. After spending months recovering from a torn ACL, simply having another defensive-line option available could be meaningful. If Reliford can work his way back into the rotation, LSU could be getting an important piece of defensive depth back at a time when every available contributor matters. Before the injury, Reliford had already begun establishing himself as a rotational piece for LSU. According to his official LSU roster bio, he appeared in 13 games as a freshman in 2024, recording 10 tackles, one tackle for loss and half a sack. He also played 156 defensive snaps that season, including a career-high 44 snaps in the Texas Bowl against Baylor. However, Reliford's development took another hit in 2025. After appearing in just four games as part of LSU's edge-rusher rotation, he suffered a season-ending rotator cuff injury against Southeastern Louisiana. How Much Could Reliford Contribute Against Texas? The biggest question surrounding Reliford isn't necessarily whether he can play, but how much LSU can realistically expect from him after such a lengthy absence. Coming back from an AC

Staff photo by Michael Johnson LSU football lost one of its starting offensive linemen to a leg injury vs. Alabama By REED DARCEY | Staff writer Reed Darcey Nov 7, 2026 Updated Nov 7, 2026 LSU right tackle Weston Davis was injured on Saturday in the third quarter of the Tigers’ 31-13 loss to Alabama. Davis, a redshirt sophomore, left the game after tight end Trey’Dez Green fell at his feet. The two-year starter couldn’t put any weight on his right leg as he was helped off the field and into the medical tent. He then hobbled to the locker room on crutches. LSU inserted Baylor transfer Sean Thompkins in Davis’ place at right tackle. Davis is a former four-star recruit who landed LSU’s starting right tackle job prior to the 2025 season. He and center Braelin Moore are the only holdover starters on the offensive line. Through eight games in 2026, Davis had allowed 21 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus data. Only two Southeastern Conference offensive linemen had surrendered more. In 2025, Davis gave up 33 pressures, which was tied for the third-most in the SEC.
